RagShortTexts: An intercepted secretary carried a letter exposing Vadomarius’s different messages to rivals.

Variants.Content: Vadomarius addressed Julian as lord and emperor but told Constantius that “your Caesar is not submissive.” Julian’s outposts detained his secretary and found the letter in a search. Those holding the intercepted document could compare the statements; people without it depended on reports.
A search establishes what text a particular bearer possessed. A soldier should not add rumor to the letter’s wording or assume that its intended emperor had already read it.

The ruler compared public deference with private correspondence. Interception changed the bargaining position, but interpretation still required sender, bearer and intended recipient; one honorific alone did not establish loyalty.
